data.title: Why the Social Security COLA is much ado about nothing
data.description:
By Mark Hulbert

Social Security's 2027 cost-of-living adjustment will be larger only if inflation is worse. Retirees better be careful what they wish for.

And they still hope for a bigger COLA. Their wish is akin to hoping for a bigger house fire so they can receive a bigger payout from their homeowners' insurance.

We don't yet know the exact COLA that Social Security will use in 2027, since it is based on the CPI levels in July, August and September of this year, and the last of these inputs won't be announced until October. The AARP is projecting that the COLA will be 3.6% - which would be the largest since the 8.7% adjustment in 2022.

The highest Social Security COLA occurred in 1980, when it was 14.3% - reflecting the double-digit increase in the consumer-price index in 1979. Just like today, Social Security beneficiaries in 1980 may have believed that, because that year's COLA was higher than in previous years, they were going to be better off than before.

They were kidding themselves, of course. They were guilty of what economists refer to as money illusion - confusing nominal dollar amounts with real, or inflation-adjusted, levels. To the extent the COLA accurately reflects inflation, your Social Security payments won't change from year to year, in real terms.

There has been a significant number of stories recently about next year's COLA. But focusing on the COLA's magnitude is much ado about nothing.

How well does the Social Security COLA reflect inflation? The accompanying chart provides an answer. It plots the annualized changes of three different series since 1982 (the first year for which data exist for all three):

-- The Social Security COLA

-- The consumer-price index for urban wage earners and clerical workers (CPI-W), the particular version of the CPI that the Social Security Administration uses to calculate its COLA

-- The consumer-price index for Americans 62 and older (CPI-E), a version of the CPI intended to reflect inflation that is uniquely endured by the elderly.

All three have produced similar annualized rates of change over the last 42 years. For example, the Social Security COLA rose at a 2.99% annualized rate between 1982 and 2025, just 9 annualized basis points greater than the CPI-E's rate of increase.

What's the real-world impact of a 9-basis-point difference in COLA? Based on the current average monthly Social Security benefit, it works out to $1.88 per month.

Rather than obsessing about the Social Security COLA, a far better use of our time would be to lobby elected representatives, urging them to ensure that the Social Security system is fully funded well into the future. As it is now, of course, beginning in 2032, the Social Security Administration will only be able to pay out 78% of the benefits to which recipients would otherwise be entitled. Based on the current average Social Security benefit, that translates to a reduction of $459 per month.

Mark Hulbert is a regular contributor to MarketWatch. His Hulbert Ratings tracks investment newsletters that pay a flat fee to be audited. He can be reached at mark@hulbertratings.com

-Mark Hulbert

data.title: There's every reason to slow AI development. But here's why it probably won't happen.
data.description:
By Brett Arends

The risks of disaster are real. But who wants to give up those massive stock valuations?

Can we trust Skynet? Or is the AI industry is playing Russian roulette with the human race?

The titans of the booming artificial-intelligence industry have sounded a three-alarm fire, warning that AI poses an existential risk to the human race and urging a global slowdown in the breakneck pace of development.

Dario Amodei, the head of $965 billion giant Anthropic and developer of the Claude AI chatbot, warned of the risks over the weekend in an extensive post on his company's website. Sam Altman, the CEO of $852 billion rival OpenAI, which owns Chat GPT, agreed. So too did Elon Musk, whose SpaceX (SPCX) empire is investing hundreds of billions of dollars in its Grok AI venture.

Some people may wonder why it took them so long to reach this point. Science-fiction writers had worked out decades ago that once super computers could think for themselves, they might no longer need us - and might no longer be our friends.

What will happen when Skynet becomes self-aware? Nobody knows. The AI industry is playing Russian roulette with the human race.

As the bestseller "If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies" pointed out last year, the companies creating these digital Frankenstein monsters don't even know how they operate.

But if there is every reason to slow AI development, there are about 40 trillion reasons why this probably won't happen.

That is the estimate of the number of dollars around the world already invested in the so-called "AI ecosystem," which is the pretentious finance way of talking about all the companies in the AI and ancillary industries.

That number, incidentally, comes from Gemini, the AI chatbot owned by Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL).

Anthropic's Claude puts the figure somewhat lower, at $25 trillion to "$30+ trillion," while OpenAI's Chat GPT puts it at $25 trillion to $30 trillion.

These include any number of household-name technology giants whose stocks have been borne aloft to epic valuations by AI hopes and ambitions. They are led by chip maker Nvidia (NVDA), now valued at more than $5 trillion, and include Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet, Meta (META), Broadcom (AVGO), Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) and others.

The valuations of these companies show up in the investment portfolios of every wealthy person in America, every rich and powerful institution, and most of the 401(k) plans of the middle class as well. Harvard University's endowment just disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX.

Big AI companies now account for about 30% of the value of the S&P 500 SPX. And that index has rocketed by an astonishing 90% in value since OpenAI launched ChatGPT nearly four years ago, igniting a market boom - or mania.

Do you think investors are going to write off these massive AI windfalls, or write them down? Most of these stocks rely on AI developing at crazy speeds just to justify the current prices, let alone any growth.

That's not to mention all those people - apparently led by President Donald Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent - who are counting on AI to produce such magical economic growth that Social Security and Medicare won't need to be cut, while taxes won't have to be restored to their 2000 balanced-budget levels.

In other words, half or most of our country - including most of the elite - are now living in castles in the air that are based, almost entirely, on dreams of magical AI that will avoid any hard choices, let alone any sacrifices on their part.

Do you think they are going to fall on their swords? Dream on.

It is no surprise that Trump rejected any calls for a slowdown, which he would consider weak and unmanly.

Oh, on a completely unrelated topic, the Trump family is looking to profit from the growth of AI - see here and here. (What were the odds?)

The Chinese government is also rejecting any idea of a slowdown.

So the chances of this happening in any meaningful way are slim at best.

The best that the rest of us can do, like unwilling participants in a game of Russian roulette, is shut our eyes and hope. Do you feel lucky?

-Brett Arends

data.title: FEMSA ADRs Rise on $280 Million Accelerated Share Repurchase Agreement
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall 




  American depositary receipts of Fomento Económico Mexicano rose after the company agreed to repurchase up to $280 million worth of American depositary shares in an accelerated share repurchase agreement. 



  ADRs were up 3.1% to $120.62 in Monday afternoon trading. They are up 19% year-to-date. 



  The Mexican retail and beverages company, also known as FEMSA, said Monday it had entered the agreement with a financial institution in the U.S.

data.title: Axiado to Demonstrate Autonomous AI Infrastructure Management at AI Infra Summit 2026
data.description:
Axiado to Demonstrate Autonomous AI Infrastructure Management at AI Infra Summit 2026

Axiado Platform Efficiency Controllers Use AI Agents to Reduce CPU, GPU and Cooling Power, Enabling Up to 30% More Tokens Per Dollar

Axiado Corporation, a leading provider of security and management solutions for modern digital infrastructure, today announced it will demonstrate its approach to autonomous AI infrastructure management at AI Infra Summit 2026, September 15–17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center in Santa Clara, California.

As AI infrastructure scales, adding more GPUs is no longer enough to overcome the physical and economic constraints facing data centers. Power, cooling, security and uptime increasingly determine how much useful AI work operators can produce from the infrastructure they’re already deploying. Axiado is addressing these challenges by moving intelligence into the management plane itself, enabling infrastructure to sense, decide and act locally at machine speed.

"The industry has hit the power wall, and you cannot buy your way out of wasting megawatts," said Gopi Sirineni, Founder, President and CEO of Axiado. "The cheapest megawatt you will ever get is the one you're already wasting. Axiado technology puts AI agents in silicon at the foundation of the platform, where they sense, decide and act in milliseconds, and turns that waste back into tokens."

At the center of Axiado’s approach is the Platform Efficiency Controller (PEC), a hardware solution built on Axiado TCU silicon. The PEC closes power and thermal management loops autonomously on the platform, using AI agents running against real-time hardware telemetry to improve efficiency without requiring a human in the loop or a round trip to centralized management software. The PEC and TCU are building blocks in Axiado’s Intelligent Hardware Management Fabric (IHMF), a broader architecture designed to extend autonomous, hardware-rooted management from individual platforms across the AI rack and upwards to fleet level.

Axiado has demonstrated measured results from autonomous agents operating on production-class systems spanning leading GPU-accelerated, Arm-based, and x86-based platforms. Two of the featured agents are:

  • Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) Agent: Delivers a 40% reduction in CPU power and a 20% reduction in GPU power by dynamically matching voltage and frequency to workload requirements.
  • Dynamic Thermal Management (DTM) Agent: Delivers a 50% reduction in air cooling power by continuously adjusting thermal management based on actual platform conditions.

These power reductions, enabled by the TCU-based Platform Efficiency Controller, translate into 10% to 30% more tokens per dollar, allowing operators to generate more useful AI output from the same infrastructure and power envelope.

Axiado Executive Presentation

At AI Infra Summit 2026, Axiado Founder, President and CEO Gopi Sirineni will present “More Tokens Per Dollar: AI-Driven Platform Efficiency Controllers for High-Density AI Racks” on Wednesday, September 16 at 3:00 p.m. PDT. During the AI Data Center Track presentation, Sirineni will discuss how autonomous platform management can improve power efficiency and AI infrastructure economics, including how Axiado’s Platform Efficiency Controller enables more tokens per dollar from the AI infrastructure operators are deploying today.

Axiado has a meeting room onsite at AI Infra Summit for briefings and video demos. Please contact press@axiado.com to set up times to meet onsite.

About Axiado

Axiado is an AI-first company redefining platform security and system management at the silicon level. Based in San Jose, Axiado partners with leading OEMs, ODMs, and CSPs worldwide. For more information, contact press@axiado.com, go to axiado.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

Ben Levine, Head of Marketing
Axiado Corporation

data.title: IRALOGIX Earns Top Industry Honor for Advancing Retirement and Wealth Integration
data.description:
IRALOGIX Earns Top Industry Honor for Advancing Retirement and Wealth Integration

2026 Wealth Management Industry Award Recognizes Company’s Unlocking Retirement/Wealth Convergence Initiative

IRALOGIX, the retirement industry’s leading fintech provider, has been named a winner of the 2026 Wealth Management Industry Awards, widely known as the “Wealthies,” for its Unlocking Retirement/Wealth Convergence initiative.

Specifically, IRALOGIX received the award for Wealth and Retirement Integration within the Retirement Plan Support and Advisor Services category. The award was presented September 10 during the 12th annual Wealth Management Industry Awards ceremony in New York City.

“This award is especially meaningful because it recognizes an opportunity we believe is becoming increasingly important for financial advisors,” said Peter de Silva, Chief Executive Officer of IRALOGIX. “Retirement has traditionally existed apart from the broader wealth relationship. Bringing those worlds closer together creates an opportunity to serve more people, deepen relationships, and rethink what retirement can contribute to a financial institution’s growth.”

The Unlocking Retirement/Wealth Convergence initiative examines how changing participant expectations and financial behaviors are creating new opportunities for advisors and financial institutions to build relationships earlier and maintain them through key financial transitions.

As retirement and wealth management become increasingly interconnected, IRALOGIX believes technology can help bridge traditional gaps between workplace retirement savings, IRAs, and broader wealth relationships. By enabling more connected experiences, financial institutions and advisors can better engage individuals across different stages of their financial lives while expanding their ability to serve retirement investors at a broader range of asset levels.

The 2026 Wealth Management Industry Awards attracted a record 1,392 nominations from 508 companies. A total of 315 companies were selected as finalists across 107 categories. An independent panel of industry judges selected winners based on the usefulness, innovation, scope, and impact of the nominated initiatives.

“The growth of the Wealthies reflects both the expanding range of organizations serving advisors and the extraordinary amount of work being done to help advisors build stronger businesses and improve outcomes for their clients,” said David Armstrong, head of editorial operations for the Wealth Management Group at Informa Connect. “To be named a finalist, and especially a winner, is meaningful recognition in a year with a record field.”

About IRALOGIX™
IRALOGIX is a retirement technology company whose pioneering cloud-native platform enables financial institutions to serve a wider range of retirement investors efficiently at scale in the $19 trillion IRA market. By anticipating industry change, IRALOGIX gives its clients the flexibility to meet rising investor expectations for simpler, more seamless retirement experiences. In doing so, IRALOGIX connects business opportunity with a broader purpose: helping more Americans pursue greater retirement security. Learn more at www.iralogix.com.

About the Wealth Management Industry Awards
The Wealth Management Industry Awards, known as the Wealthies, recognize organizations and individuals supporting financial advisor success through innovation, leadership, and service. Produced by Wealth Management, the annual program recognizes achievement across the wealth management industry.

data.title: Battery Global Advisors Closes $208 Million in Capital Commitments for its Digital Infrastructure Fund
data.description:
Battery Global Advisors Closes $208 Million in Capital Commitments for its Digital Infrastructure Fund

Battery Global Advisors ("BGA"), an investment firm providing customized wealth management within an institutional family office framework, today announced the final closing of the BGA Digital Infrastructure Fund ("DIF"), with $208.5 million in total capital commitments. DIF invests in data center and digital infrastructure assets at the corporate layer of the infrastructure value chain, targeting platforms with contracted revenue, secured power, and established assets.

DIF exceeded its $150 million target following support from institutions, technology entrepreneurs, and venture capital and private equity executives. To date, the Fund has committed capital to five portfolio companies, representing approximately 40% of total commitments. The near-term investment pipeline remains active, with several opportunities currently in late-stage diligence. BGA engaged PJT Park Hill as the placement agent for DIF and other digital infrastructure engagements.

Since 2024, BGA has committed more than $900 million to the digital infrastructure sector across its fund and co-investment vehicles. BGA's opportunistic mandate allows the firm to pursue niche, high-growth opportunities that fall outside the constraints of traditional institutional mandates, and its relationships across the technology community have made it a preferred capital provider for management teams and development partners.

“We built DIF with the flexibility to pursue our highest-conviction opportunities wherever they sit in the digital infrastructure ecosystem,” said Brandon Colón, Chief Investment Officer of Battery Global Advisors. “The mandate lets us underwrite situations that fall outside traditional institutional boxes, and given the growing complexity of financing needs, makes us an attractive partner to management teams and developers.”

“We are grateful for the confidence our investors have placed in the Fund. DIF is well positioned to support the evolving digital infrastructure build-out given BGA’s strong history within the real estate, venture, and technology communities,” said John O’Connor, Chief Executive Officer of Battery Global Advisors. “Exceeding our target with support from this investor base tells us our platform and strategy resonate with the market.”

About Battery Global Advisors

Battery Global Advisors provides customized wealth management within an institutional family office framework. BGA manages over $7.6 billion in assets for venture capital and private equity executives and technology entrepreneurs, blending traditional wealth management with access to a diverse set of investment opportunities. “BGA Digital Infrastructure Fund” is the marketing name for BGA Private Opportunities Fund, LLC – Digital Infrastructure Series. BGA is based in Boston, MA. For more information, please visit www.bga.com.

Bronson Green, Director, Strategy & Operations
Battery Global Advisors, LLC

data.title: Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Encourages FuelCell Energy, Inc. (FCEL) Shareholders To Inquire About Securities Fraud Class Action
data.description:
Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Encourages FuelCell Energy, Inc. (FCEL) Shareholders To Inquire About Securities Fraud Class Action

Law Offices of Howard G. Smith announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed on behalf of investors who purchased FuelCell Energy, Inc. (“FuelCell” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: FCEL) securities between June 24, 2026 and September 1, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). FuelCell investors have until November 10, 2026 to file a lead plaintiff motion.

IF YOU ARE AN INVESTOR WHO SUFFERED A LOSS IN FUELCELL ENERGY, INC. (FCEL), CONTACT THE LAW OFFICES OF HOWARD G. SMITH TO PARTICIPATE IN THE ONGOING SECURITIES FRAUD LAWSUIT.

Contact the Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to discuss your legal rights by email at howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, by telephone at (215) 638-4847 or visit our website at www.howardsmithlaw.com.

What Happened?

On September 2, 2026, before the market opened, FuelCell reported its fiscal third quarter 2026 financial results, reporting a net loss of $45.3 million. According to the Company’s press release, this reflected “a higher gross loss than the prior year period,” which was caused by “product costs and manufacturing overhead that currently exceed the contractual pricing established under the CEPA with Fit Energy.” Further, FuelCell reported that the annualized production rate was “below the production volume at which we expect our cost structure to align with market-based pricing for orders of this scale,” and as a result, the Company recorded a $17 million charge to “reflect the impact of contractual pricing provisions associated with specific inventory and firm purchase commitments” arising from Phase 0 of the CEPA.

On this news, FuelCell shares fell $2.68, or 15.69%, to close at $14.40 per share on September 2, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

What Is The Lawsuit About?

The complaint filed in this class action alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that the Company’s manufacturing capacity was inadequate to generate the production rate required under the CEPA; (2) that, as a result, the Company’s annualized production rate for deliveries under the CEPA with Fit Energy was slower than expected; (3) that, as a result, the Company was incurring higher product costs and manufacturing overhead expenses; (4) that, as a result of the slower production rate, the Company was reasonably likely to incur charges in connection with the CEPA; (5) that the foregoing was a known trend affecting the Company’s profitability; and (6) that, as a result of the foregoing, Defendants’ positive statements about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

data.title: TransAlta Ordered by U.S. Government to Keep Washington Coal Unit Online for 90 More Days
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese 




  TransAlta has received another order from the U.S. Department of Energy to keep Washington state's last coal-fired power plant operational for an additional 90 days. 



  The Calgary, Alberta-based power generator said Monday that its subsidiary TransAlta Centralia Generation received the order from federal regulators mandating that Unit 2 of its Centralia Generating Station remain available to support the grid. 



  The station is now ordered to remain available for operations until Dec. 12. 



  The power station was earmarked for closure at the end of 2025 as part of a shift toward cleaner sources to generate power but has received three other requests to keep the plant operational. The company had already retired Unit 1 at the end of 2020 as part of a state mandated two-phase closure of the coal-fired plant. 



  TransAlta said Monday that it will continue to comply with the directive while coordinating with state and federal officials.

data.title: Waymo Launches Robotaxis in Las Vegas
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton 




  Waymo has added Las Vegas to its repertoire of cities where its self-driving cabs are available. 



  The robotaxi company, which is owned by Alphabet, said Monday it is now providing fully autonomous rides to the public in the popular Nevada city. 



  Waymo plans to give increasing access to more riders in Clark County, Nev., as it works toward opening its services to everyone. 



  Earlier this month, Waymo launched driverless rides in Denver, San Diego and Tampa, Fla. 



  Competitors including Tesla and Amazon's Zoox have also been ramping up the number of cities where they operate.
